label: February 2–8
title: “The Lord Called His People Zion” —  Moses 7

items.text: Throughout history, people have strived to build an ideal society free from poverty and violence. As God’s people, we share this desire, calling it building Zion. This involves caring for the needy, promoting peace, making covenants, and dwelling in righteousness, becoming one with each other and with Jesus Christ, the King of Zion.

Zion is not merely a geographical location or a city; it is a state of the heart and spirit. The Lord has taught that Zion is comprised of ‘the pure in heart.’ Therefore, the most effective way to build Zion is to begin by cultivating purity in our own hearts and within our homes.

The Prophet Joseph Smith was inspired by Enoch and his City of Holiness, knowing the day had come to reestablish Zion on earth. This realization ignited a lifelong quest to build Zion. Studying Moses 7 can inspire us today to continue this vital effort.

To understand Zion, we must ask, 'What is Zion?' and 'How does it differ from the rest of the world?' Consider the answers found in Moses 7, especially verses 16–21, 27, 53, and 62–69. These will reveal the work still needed to build Zion.

Reflect on times when you have felt ‘of one heart and one mind’ with others. What actions did people take to create such righteous unity? These experiences offer valuable insights into how we can build Zion, fostering a spirit of togetherness and shared purpose.

Jesus Christ is unequivocally ‘the King of Zion.’ Understanding what it means to have Him as our King, and recognizing His other divine titles mentioned in this verse, offers profound insights into His nature and our path to entering Zion through Him.

Enoch's vision in Moses 7 reveals a God who is deeply emotionally invested in His children, weeping with sorrow and rejoicing with gladness. This understanding challenges the notion of a distant deity, showing us a compassionate and loving Heavenly Father.

Despite experiencing ‘bitterness’ in life, Enoch’s vision teaches us to ‘lift up your heart, and be glad.’ By observing God’s reasons for rejoicing, we can learn to find joy and hope, even amidst challenges, and embrace the uplifting power of the gospel.

Moses 7 contains one of history’s earliest prophecies of the Savior’s Second Coming. The description of the last days in verses 59–67 is remarkable. Reflecting on how these prophecies are being fulfilled reveals God’s ongoing, purposeful work in the latter days.

God desires for His people to be ‘of one heart and one mind.’ This profound unity is a hallmark of Zion. By striving for this oneness, we align ourselves with God’s will and create a community that reflects His love and purpose.
